name: 1. Simple Subject Sorting
description: A great starting point. Sorts images into folders based on common subjects found in their captions.
scheme:
# This is a basic scheme that uses the .txt files from the Image Captioner node.
# It's perfect for getting a quick, high-level organization of your images.

# --- Sort by Subject ---
captionfile_contains: person -> By_Subject/People
captionfile_contains: man -> By_Subject/People
captionfile_contains: woman -> By_Subject/People
captionfile_contains: cat -> By_Subject/Animals/Cats
captionfile_contains: dog -> By_Subject/Animals/Dogs
captionfile_contains: car -> By_Subject/Vehicles
captionfile_contains: landscape -> By_Subject/Landscapes

# --- Sort by Style ---
captionfile_contains: photo -> By_Style/Photography
captionfile_contains: anime -> By_Style/Anime
captionfile_contains: painting -> By_Style/Paintings

# --- Sort by File Type ---
filename_contains: screenshot -> By_Type/Screenshots
filename_contains: test -> By_Type/_Tests

name: 2. Dataset Creation
description: For LoRA trainers. Sorts images into detailed categories based on content, style, and composition.
scheme:
# This scheme is designed for creating well-organized datasets for training.
# It prioritizes detailed content descriptions from caption files.

# --- Sort by Composition ---
captionfile_contains: portrait -> By_Composition/Portraits
captionfile_contains: close-up -> By_Composition/Close_Ups
captionfile_contains: full body -> By_Composition/Full_Body_Shots
captionfile_contains: wide shot -> By_Composition/Wide_Shots

# --- Sort by Subject ---
captionfile_contains: 1girl -> By_Subject/1girl
captionfile_contains: 1boy -> By_Subject/1boy
# Add your character's trigger word here:
# captionfile_contains: my_character_trigger -> By_Subject/My_Character

# --- Sort by Style ---
captionfile_contains: anime -> By_Style/Anime
captionfile_contains: realistic -> By_Style/Realistic
captionfile_contains: painting -> By_Style/Painting
captionfile_contains: sketch -> By_Style/Sketch

# --- Sort by Resolution (useful for bucketing) ---
image_resolution: ==1024x1024 -> By_Resolution/1024x1024
image_resolution: ==768x1024 -> By_Resolution/768x1024
image_resolution: ==512x512 -> By_Resolution/512x512
image_resolution: ==512x768 -> By_Resolution/512x768

name: 3. Workflow Archiving (Technical)
description: For experimenters. Sorts images based on the specific models, samplers, and LoRAs used to create them.
scheme:
# This scheme uses the `metadata_contains` rule to read the saved workflow in your PNGs.
# It's perfect for comparing results and archiving your experiments.

# --- Sort by Workflow Type ---
metadata_contains: AnimateDiff -> By_Workflow/AnimateDiff
metadata_contains: SVD -> By_Workflow/SVD

# --- Sort by Sampler & Scheduler ---
metadata_contains: dpmpp_2m_sde -> By_Sampler/dpmpp_2m_sde
metadata_contains: euler_ancestral -> By_Sampler/euler_ancestral
metadata_contains: karras -> By_Scheduler/karras

# --- Sort by Checkpoint Model ---
# Uncomment and edit these lines with your model names.
# metadata_contains: Juggernaut.safetensors -> By_Model/Juggernaut
# metadata_contains: Dreamshaper.safetensors -> By_Model/Dreamshaper

# --- Sort by LoRA ---
# Uncomment and edit these lines with your LoRA filenames.
# metadata_contains: my_character_lora.safetensors -> By_LoRA/My_Character
# metadata_contains: my_style_lora.safetensors -> By_LoRA/My_Style

# --- Sort by ControlNet ---
# Uncomment and edit these lines with your ControlNet model names.
# metadata_contains: control_v11p_sd15_openpose -> By_ControlNet/OpenPose
# metadata_contains: control_v11f1p_sd15_depth -> By_ControlNet/Depth

name: 4. AI vs. Photos Sorting
description: A very useful scheme to separate AI-generated images from regular photos in a mixed folder.
scheme:
# This scheme intelligently separates images that have ComfyUI workflow metadata from those that don't.
# It's the perfect way to clean up a folder containing both your generations and your personal photos.

# Rule 1: If an image contains ComfyUI workflow data, it's an AI generation.
# The `prompt_keyword` criterion is a fast way to check for a KSampler or CLIPTextEncode node.
metadata_contains: KSampler -> AI_Generated
metadata_contains: CLIPTextEncode -> AI_Generated

# Rule 2: If an image has a caption file created by the Captioner node, it's also likely an AI image.
captionfile_contains: 1girl -> AI_Generated/By_Subject
captionfile_contains: 1boy -> AI_Generated/By_Subject

# Rule 3: If a file is a video, sort it into a separate video folder.
# This rule is implicitly handled by the fallback, but can be explicit.
# Note: This requires file extensions to be supported by the node.

# The 'fallback_folder' setting for the node will catch everything else.
# Set the fallback_folder to 'My_Photos' to automatically sort all non-AI images there.

name: 5. Project-Based Sorting
description: Organizes files into project folders based on keywords in filenames or captions.
scheme:
# This scheme is for artists and designers working on multiple projects at once.
# Edit the keywords and project folder names to match your work.

# --- Project: Dragon's Lair (Fantasy) ---
filename_contains: proj_dragon -> Projects/Dragon_Lair
captionfile_contains: fantasy dragon -> Projects/Dragon_Lair

# --- Project: Neo-Kyoto (Cyberpunk) ---
filename_contains: proj_neokyoto -> Projects/Neo-Kyoto_2077
captionfile_contains: cyberpunk city -> Projects/Neo-Kyoto_2077
captionfile_contains: neon alley -> Projects/Neo-Kyoto_2077

# --- Project: Forest Spirit (Nature) ---
filename_contains: proj_forest -> Projects/Forest_Spirit
captionfile_contains: magical forest -> Projects/Forest_Spirit

# --- General Categories for non-project files ---
filename_contains: test -> _Tests
filename_contains: experiment -> _Tests

name: 6. Sort by Aspect Ratio
description: Groups images by common aspect ratios (Square, Widescreen, Portrait).
scheme:
# This scheme uses the `image_resolution` rule with `==` to sort by exact dimensions, which is a great way to group by aspect ratio.

# --- Square (1:1) ---
image_resolution: ==1024x1024 -> By_AspectRatio/Square
image_resolution: ==512x512 -> By_AspectRatio/Square

# --- Widescreen (16:9) ---
image_resolution: ==1920x1080 -> By_AspectRatio/Widescreen_16_9
image_resolution: ==1280x720 -> By_AspectRatio/Widescreen_16_9
image_resolution: ==1024x576 -> By_AspectRatio/Widescreen_16_9

# --- Portrait (2:3 or 3:4) ---
image_resolution: ==512x768 -> By_AspectRatio/Portrait_2_3
image_resolution: ==768x1024 -> By_AspectRatio/Portrait_3_4

# --- Ultrawide (21:9) ---
# image_resolution: ==1344x576 -> By_AspectRatio/Ultrawide_21_9

# --- High-Resolution Fallback ---
image_resolution: >1920x1080 -> By_Resolution/High_Resolution

name: 7. Comprehensive Library (Hybrid)
description: The ultimate sorting scheme. Combines technical, content, and resolution rules for a meticulously organized library.
scheme:
# This is an advanced, hierarchical scheme that sorts files with multiple passes.
# The order of rules is important, as the first match wins.

# 1. First, separate special workflow types like animations and videos.
metadata_contains: AnimateDiff -> Library/AI_Creations/Animations
metadata_contains: SVD -> Library/AI_Creations/Animations

# 2. Next, sort by the primary model used to create the image.
# Uncomment and edit with your favorite model names.
# metadata_contains: Juggernaut.safetensors -> Library/AI_Creations/By_Model/Juggernaut
# metadata_contains: Dreamshaper.safetensors -> Library/AI_Creations/By_Model/Dreamshaper

# 3. Then, sort by the main subject matter using caption files.
# This creates subject folders inside the main library.
captionfile_contains: portrait -> Library/By_Subject/Portraits
captionfile_contains: landscape -> Library/By_Subject/Landscapes
captionfile_contains: cat -> Library/By_Subject/Animals/Cats
captionfile_contains: dog -> Library/By_Subject/Animals/Dogs

# 4. Separate out any non-AI photos into their own top-level folder.
# This rule is implicitly handled by setting the node's 'fallback_folder' to 'Library/My_Photos'.

# 5. Finally, use resolution as a fallback for anything not yet sorted.
image_resolution: >1920x1080 -> Library/By_Resolution/High_Resolution
image_resolution: <1024x768 -> Library/By_Resolution/Low_Resolution

# 6. Put test images in their own folder.
filename_contains: test -> Library/_Tests
